subject: alkali fly
title: This Fly Walks Underwater Inside Its Own Air Bubble, 15 Minutes a Dive

scenes.text: This fly goes scuba diving. It brings its own tank.
The alkali fly of Mono Lake, California, water three times saltier than the sea.
Dense hairs and a waxy coat trap a bubble of air around it when it crawls under.
It walks the lake bed for up to 15 minutes, eating algae and laying eggs, then lets go and floats up.
Mark Twain wrote that you can hold them under as long as you please. They don't mind.
Fifteen minutes under, and it climbs out bone dry.

description:
The alkali fly of Mono Lake crawls underwater wrapped in a bubble of air and comes out dry.
A 2017 study in PNAS by Floris van Breugel and Michael Dickinson of Caltech found that the fly's unusually dense hairs and waxy cuticle trap an air bubble that works as an external lung. The flies crawl to depths of 4 to 8 metres and spend up to 15 minutes underwater grazing algae and laying eggs, in water three times saltier than the Pacific with a pH of 10. Pushing through the surface takes about 18 times the fly's body weight. Mark Twain described them in Roughing It in 1872, and the flies feed more than 80 species of migrating birds.
Which animal has the strangest way of breathing?
